The V110E1004 is an angle-pattern thermostatic radiator valve body from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 1/2 inch, rated 4.6 Cv and built to the high-capacity design.

A thermostatic radiator valve gives one radiator its own temperature control without any wiring. The head senses room air and opens or closes the valve underneath it, so a south-facing room that runs hot stops taking heat while the rest of the loop keeps running.

Pattern matters more than it sounds. A angle body is chosen to suit how the pipe arrives at the radiator: straight where the supply runs in line with the valve, angle where it turns up out of the floor, horizontal angle where it comes through the wall and has to turn in plan rather than in elevation. Fitting the wrong pattern means re-piping, not re-orienting.

The 4.6 Cv rating is what sizes the valve to the radiator. Too small and the radiator starves at design temperature; too large and the head loses authority, hunting between too hot and too cold instead of holding a setting.

What a working TRV takes: a valve body and a thermostatic head, ordered separately. This listing is the body.

The T104A1040 is a thermostatic radiator actuator from Resideo (Honeywell Home). It is the head that sits on the radiator valve and holds the room at the temperature set on the dial, with no power and no wiring.

The mechanism is a sealed charge that expands as the room warms and pushes the valve closed. Because it is entirely mechanical, it keeps working through a power cut and it never needs a battery — which is why TRVs are still specified on hydronic systems that have every other control electronic.

The high-capacity design matches the high-capacity valve bodies, which move considerably more water than a standard TRV. On a large cast-iron radiator or a long run of baseboard, standard capacity is the reason a zone never quite catches up on a cold morning.

What a working TRV takes: a valve body and a thermostatic head, ordered separately. This listing is the head.

The V110D1000 is a straight-pattern thermostatic radiator valve body from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 1/2 inch, rated 4.6 Cv and built to the high-capacity design.

A thermostatic radiator valve gives one radiator its own temperature control without any wiring. The head senses room air and opens or closes the valve underneath it, so a south-facing room that runs hot stops taking heat while the rest of the loop keeps running.

Pattern matters more than it sounds. A straight body is chosen to suit how the pipe arrives at the radiator: straight where the supply runs in line with the valve, angle where it turns up out of the floor, horizontal angle where it comes through the wall and has to turn in plan rather than in elevation. Fitting the wrong pattern means re-piping, not re-orienting.

The 4.6 Cv rating is what sizes the valve to the radiator. Too small and the radiator starves at design temperature; too large and the head loses authority, hunting between too hot and too cold instead of holding a setting.

The T100B1035 is a thermostatic radiator actuator from Resideo (Honeywell Home). It is the head that sits on the radiator valve and holds the room at the temperature set on the dial, with no power and no wiring.

The mechanism is a sealed charge that expands as the room warms and pushes the valve closed. Because it is entirely mechanical, it keeps working through a power cut and it never needs a battery — which is why TRVs are still specified on hydronic systems that have every other control electronic.

This head uses a remote sensor. The sensing element sits on a capillary away from the valve, which matters when the valve is behind a cover, under a deep sill, or low to the floor — anywhere the air around the valve is not the air the room is actually at. A head sensing its own radiator reads hot and shuts the radiator down early.
